sanskrit: hiṃsāvihārī satatam aviśeṣaguṇāguṇaḥ bahvalīko manasvī ca lubdho 'tyarthaṃ nṛśaṃsakṛt
english: He who takes his pleasure forever in cruelty, who draws no distinction between virtue and vice, who is full of falsehood, headstrong, exceedingly greedy, and a doer of pitiless deeds—such a one is known as cruel.

sanskrit: dharmaśīlaṃ guṇopetaṃ pāpa ity avagacchati ātmaśīlānumānena na viśvasiti kasya cit
english: He takes a man of righteous conduct, endowed with virtues, to be wicked; judging others by the measure of his own disposition, he trusts no one at all.

sanskrit: pareṣāṃ yatra doṣaḥ syāt tad guhyaṃ saṃprakāśayet samāneṣv eva doṣeṣu vṛttyartham upaghātayet
english: Wherever there is a fault in others, that secret he makes public; and though their faults be no greater than his own, he ruins them for his own advantage.

sanskrit: tathopakāriṇaṃ caiva manyate vañcitaṃ param dattvāpi ca dhanaṃ kāle saṃtapaty upakāriṇe
english: He reckons one who has done him a kindness to be merely a dupe; and even after giving wealth in time of need, he grieves over it toward his benefactor.

sanskrit: bhakṣyaṃ bhojyam atho lehyaṃ yac cānyat sādhu bhojanam prekṣamāṇeṣu yo 'śnīyān nṛśaṃsa iti taṃ viduḥ
english: He who would eat the things to be chewed, the things to be swallowed, the things to be licked, and whatever other goodly food, while others look on hungry—him they know to be cruel.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇebhyaḥ pradāyāgraṃ yaḥ suhṛdbhiḥ sahāśnute sa pretya labhate svargam iha cānantyam aśnute
english: But he who first gives the choicest portion to the brāhmaṇas and then eats together with his friends—he gains heaven hereafter, and even here enjoys an unending abundance.

sanskrit: eṣa te bharataśreṣṭha nṛśaṃsaḥ parikīrtitaḥ sadā vivarjanīyo vai puruṣeṇa bubhūṣatā
english: Thus, O best of the Bharatas, has the cruel man been described to you; he is ever to be shunned by any man who wishes to fare well.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca kṛtārtho yakṣyamāṇaś ca sarvavedāntagaś ca yaḥ ācāryapitṛbhāryārthaṃ svādhyāyārtham athāpi vā
english: Bhīṣma said: One whose purpose is accomplished, who is about to perform sacrifice, who has mastered the whole of the Vedānta, and who seeks alms for the sake of his teacher, his ancestors, his wife, or for the sake of his own recitation of the sacred texts—

sanskrit: ete vai sādhavo dṛṣṭā brāhmaṇā dharmabhikṣavaḥ asvebhyo deyam etebhyo dānaṃ vidyāviśeṣataḥ
english: these are seen to be worthy brāhmaṇas who beg for the sake of righteousness; to them a gift should be given even from what is not one's own surplus, in proportion to their special learning.

sanskrit: anyatra dakṣiṇā yā tu deyā bharatasattama anyebhyo hi bahirvedyāṃ nākṛtānnaṃ vidhīyate
english: Apart from these, O best of the Bharatas, the sacrificial fee that is to be given is given to others outside the altar; but uncooked food is not ordained for them.

sanskrit: sarvaratnāni rājā ca yathārhaṃ pratipādayet brāhmaṇāś caiva yajñāś ca sahānnāḥ sahadakṣiṇāḥ
english: The king should bestow all manner of precious things, each as is fitting; and the brāhmaṇas and the sacrifices alike should be furnished with food and with sacrificial fees.

sanskrit: yasya traivārṣikaṃ bhaktaṃ paryāptaṃ bhṛtyavṛttaye adhikaṃ vāpi vidyeta sa somaṃ pātum arhati
english: He whose store of food is sufficient for three years to maintain his dependents, or even more than that, is fit to drink the soma.

sanskrit: yajñaś cet pratividdhaḥ syād aṅgenaikena yajvanaḥ brāhmaṇasya viśeṣeṇa dhārmike sati rājani
english: If the sacrifice of a sacrificer—especially of a brāhmaṇa—should be hindered in but a single one of its parts, while the king is a righteous one,

sanskrit: yo vaiśyaḥ syād bahupaśur hīnakratur asomapaḥ kuṭumbāt tasya tad dravyaṃ yajñārthaṃ pārthivo haret
english: then, if there be a vaiśya rich in cattle who performs no rites and drinks no soma, the king may take from that man's household the wealth needed for the sacrifice.

sanskrit: āhared veśmataḥ kiṃ cit kāmaṃ śūdrasya dravyataḥ na hi veśmani śūdrasya kaś cid asti parigrahaḥ
english: He may take somewhat, if he wishes, from the dwelling and the goods of a śūdra; for in a śūdra's house there exists no possession that may not be taken.

sanskrit: yo 'nāhitāgniḥ śatagur ayajvā ca sahasraguḥ tayor api kuṭumbābhyām āhared avicārayan
english: From one who has not set up the sacred fires though he owns a hundred cattle, and from one who performs no sacrifices though he owns a thousand—from the households of both of these the king may take without hesitation.

sanskrit: adātṛbhyo haren nityaṃ vyākhyāpya nṛpatiḥ prabho tathā hy ācarato dharmo nṛpateḥ syād athākhilaḥ
english: From those who will not give, the king may ever take, O lord, after making his purpose known; for by acting thus the whole duty of a king is fulfilled.

sanskrit: tathaiva saptame bhakte bhaktāni ṣaḍ anaśnatā aśvastanavidhānena hartavyaṃ hīnakarmaṇaḥ khalāt kṣetrāt tathāgārād yato vāpy upapadyate
english: Likewise one who, fasting through six meals, must eat at the seventh, may, by the rule of one who lays up no store for the morrow, take from the niggard who neglects his rites—from his field, from his house, or from wherever it may be had.

sanskrit: ākhyātavyaṃ nṛpasyaitat pṛcchato 'pṛcchato 'pi vā na tasmai dhārayed daṇḍaṃ rājā dharmeṇa dharmavit
english: This should be declared to the king, whether he asks or asks not; and the king who knows the law should not, in accordance with righteousness, lay any punishment upon such a one.

sanskrit: kṣatriyasya hi bāliśyād brāhmaṇaḥ kliśyate kṣudhā śrutaśīle samājñāya vṛttim asya prakalpayet athainaṃ parirakṣeta pitā putram ivaurasam
english: If through the folly of a kṣatriya a brāhmaṇa is afflicted by hunger, the king, having learned of the man's learning and conduct, should provide him a livelihood, and should thereafter protect him as a father protects his own begotten son.

sanskrit: iṣṭiṃ vaiśvānarīṃ nityaṃ nirvaped abdaparyaye avikalpaḥ purādharmo dharmavādais tu kevalam
english: At the close of each year he should ever offer the Vaiśvānara oblation; the ancient law admits of no alternative, save only in the disputations of those who debate the law.

sanskrit: viśvais tu devaiḥ sādhyaiś ca brāhmaṇaiś ca maharṣibhiḥ āpatsu maraṇād bhītair liṅgapratinidhiḥ kṛtaḥ
english: Yet by the Viśvedevas, the Sādhyas, the brāhmaṇas, and the great sages, in seasons of distress, fearing death, a substitute that bears only the outward sign was sanctioned.

sanskrit: prabhuḥ prathamakalpasya yo 'nukalpena vartate na sāṃparāyikaṃ tasya durmater vidyate phalam
english: But he who, though capable of the primary rule, conducts himself by the secondary expedient—for that man of evil mind there is found no reward in the world to come.

sanskrit: na brāhmaṇān vedayeta kaś cid rājani mānavaḥ avīryo vedanād vidyāt suvīryo vīryavattaram
english: No man should denounce brāhmaṇas before the king; one of little power, by such denouncing, would learn his own weakness, and one of great power his still greater strength.

sanskrit: tasmād rājñā sadā tejo duḥsahaṃ brahmavādinām mantā śāstā vidhātā ca brāhmaṇo deva ucyate tasmin nākuśalaṃ brūyān na śuktām īrayed giram
english: Therefore the king must hold the splendor of those who expound the sacred word to be unbearable; the brāhmaṇa is called the deviser, the chastiser, and the ordainer—a very god; to him one should speak no unkind word, nor utter any bitter speech.

sanskrit: kṣatriyo bāhuvīryeṇa taraty āpadam ātmanaḥ dhanena vaiśyaḥ śūdraś ca mantrair homaiś ca vai dvijaḥ
english: The kṣatriya crosses over his own calamity by the strength of his arms; the vaiśya and the śūdra by their wealth; and the twice-born by his sacred formulas and his oblations.

sanskrit: na vai kanyā na yuvatir nāmantro na ca bāliśaḥ pariveṣṭāgnihotrasya bhaven nāsaṃskṛtas tathā narake nipatanty ete juhvānāḥ sa ca yasya tat
english: Neither a maiden, nor a young woman, nor one ignorant of the sacred formulas, nor a fool, nor an uninitiated man should be the server at the Agnihotra; for those who make the offering thus fall into hell, together with him whose rite it is.

sanskrit: prājāpatyam adattvāśvam agnyādheyasya dakṣiṇām anāhitāgnir iti sa procyate dharmadarśibhiḥ
english: He who, at the establishing of the fires, has not given a horse as the Prājāpatya sacrificial fee is declared by those who perceive the law to be one who has not set up the fires.

sanskrit: puṇyāny anyāni kurvīta śraddadhāno jitendriyaḥ anāptadakṣiṇair yajñair na yajeta kathaṃ cana
english: Faithful and master of his senses, let him perform other meritorious acts; but with sacrifices whose fees are not fully rendered let him by no means sacrifice.

sanskrit: prajāḥ paśūṃś ca svargaṃ ca hanti yajño hy adakṣiṇaḥ indriyāṇi yaśaḥ kīrtim āyuś cāsyopakṛntati
english: A sacrifice without its fee destroys offspring, cattle, and heaven; it cuts away the senses, the renown, the fame, and the very life of him who offers it.

sanskrit: udakyā hy āsate ye ca ye ca ke cid anagnayaḥ kulaṃ cāśrotriyaṃ yeṣāṃ sarve te śūdradharmiṇaḥ
english: Those households where the women dwell in their courses unregarded, those that keep no sacred fires, and those families in which the Veda is not studied—all these follow the law of śūdras.

sanskrit: udapānodake grāme brāhmaṇo vṛṣalīpatiḥ uṣitvā dvādaśa samāḥ śūdrakarmeha gacchati
english: A brāhmaṇa who becomes the husband of a śūdra woman, dwelling for twelve years in a village whose only water is from a well, sinks here into the condition of a śūdra in his works.

sanskrit: anāryāṃ śayane bibhrad ujjhan bibhrac ca yo dvijām abrāhmaṇo manyamānas tṛṇeṣv āsīta pṛṣṭhataḥ tathā sa śudhyate rājañ śṛṇu cātra vaco mama
english: He who keeps an ignoble woman in his bed, casting off and forsaking his brāhmaṇa wife, should, no longer accounting himself a brāhmaṇa, sit behind the others upon the grass; thus, O king, is he purified—and hear in this matter my words.

sanskrit: yad ekarātreṇa karoti pāpaṃ; kṛṣṇaṃ varṇaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ sevamānaḥ sthānāsanābhyāṃ vicaran vratī saṃs; tribhir varṣaiḥ śamayed ātmapāpam
english: The sin which a brāhmaṇa commits in a single night by consorting with a woman of the black caste, he should expiate in three years, passing his time standing and seated by turns and bound by his vow, and so quell the sin of his soul.

sanskrit: na narmayuktaṃ vacanaṃ hinasti; na strīṣu rājan na vivāhakāle na gurvarthe nātmano jīvitārthe; pañcānṛtāny āhur apātakāni
english: A word spoken in jest does no harm, O king, nor one spoken to women, nor at the time of a marriage, nor for a teacher's sake, nor to save one's own life: these five untruths the wise declare to be no sins.

sanskrit: śraddadhānaḥ śubhāṃ vidyāṃ hīnād api samācaret suvarṇam api cāmedhyād ādadīteti dhāraṇā
english: With faith one may receive auspicious knowledge even from a man of low birth, and gold even from filth—such is the settled doctrine.

sanskrit: strīratnaṃ duṣkulāc cāpi viṣād apy amṛtaṃ pibet aduṣṭā hi striyo ratnam āpa ity eva dharmataḥ
english: A jewel of a woman may be taken even from a base family, and the nectar of immortality may be drunk even out of poison; for women undefiled are jewels, pure as water—so it is by the law.

sanskrit: gobrāhmaṇahitārthaṃ ca varṇānāṃ saṃkareṣu ca gṛhṇīyāt tu dhanur vaiśyaḥ paritrāṇāya cātmanaḥ
english: For the welfare of cattle and brāhmaṇas, and when the castes are thrown into confusion, and for the saving of his own life, even a vaiśya may take up the bow.

sanskrit: surāpānaṃ brahmahatyā gurutalpam athāpi vā anirdeśyāni manyante prāṇāntānīti dhāraṇā
english: The drinking of liquor, the slaying of a brāhmaṇa, and the defiling of a teacher's bed are deemed beyond all enumeration, and the doctrine holds them to be sins that endure to the very end of life.

sanskrit: suvarṇaharaṇaṃ stainyaṃ viprāsaṅgaś ca pātakam viharan madyapānaṃ cāpy agamyāgamanaṃ tathā
english: The theft of gold, robbery, and the seduction of a brāhmaṇa's wife are grievous sins; so too is the open drinking of strong drink, and intercourse with women forbidden to a man.

sanskrit: patitaiḥ saṃprayogāc ca brāhmaṇair yonitas tathā acireṇa mahārāja tādṛśo vai bhavaty uta
english: And through union with brāhmaṇas who have fallen, and through alliance by marriage with them, O great king, a man very soon becomes such as they are.

sanskrit: saṃvatsareṇa patati patitena sahācaran yājanādhyāpanād yaunān na tu yānāsanāśanāt
english: By a year's association with a fallen man one becomes fallen—through officiating at his sacrifices, teaching him, or marriage ties with him, but not merely through riding, sitting, or eating with him.

sanskrit: etāni ca tato 'nyāni nirdeśyānīti dhāraṇā nirdeśyakena vidhinā kālenāvyasanī bhavet
english: These sins, and others besides, are held to be of the kind that can be defined and atoned; by the prescribed rule, in due time, and free from addiction to them, a man becomes purified.

sanskrit: annaṃ tiryaṅ na hotavyaṃ pretakarmaṇy apātite triṣu tv eteṣu pūrveṣu na kurvīta vicāraṇām
english: Food should not be offered crosswise to the fire, nor at a funeral rite for one not yet fallen; but in those three former cases one should make no debate.

sanskrit: amātyān vā gurūn vāpi jahyād dharmeṇa dhārmikaḥ prāyaścittam akurvāṇair naitair arhati saṃvidam
english: A righteous man may, in accordance with the law, forsake even ministers or teachers; with such men, who perform no expiation, he ought to hold no compact.

sanskrit: adharmakārī dharmeṇa tapasā hanti kilbiṣam bruvan stena iti stenaṃ tāvat prāpnoti kilbiṣam astenaṃ stena ity uktvā dviguṇaṃ pāpam āpnuyāt
english: A doer of wrong destroys his guilt by righteousness and austerity; and he who calls a thief a thief incurs but so much guilt, while he who calls one who is no thief a thief incurs twice the sin.

sanskrit: tribhāgaṃ brahmahatyāyāḥ kanyā prāpnoti duṣyatī yas tu dūṣayitā tasyāḥ śeṣaṃ prāpnoti kilbiṣam
english: A maiden who lets herself be defiled incurs a third part of the guilt of slaying a brāhmaṇa; but he who defiles her incurs the remaining portion of the sin.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāyāvagūryeha spṛṣṭvā gurutaraṃ bhavet varṣāṇāṃ hi śataṃ pāpaḥ pratiṣṭhāṃ nādhigacchati
english: To raise a weapon against a brāhmaṇa here is a sin, and to touch him with it is heavier still; for a hundred years the sinner finds no firm standing.

sanskrit: sahasraṃ tv eva varṣāṇāṃ nipātya narake vaset tasmān naivāvagūryād dhi naiva jātu nipātayet
english: And he who actually strikes him down must dwell a thousand years in hell; therefore one should never even raise a weapon against him, nor ever strike him down.

sanskrit: śoṇitaṃ yāvataḥ pāṃsūn saṃgṛhṇīyād dvijakṣatāt tāvatīḥ sa samā rājan narake parivartate
english: As many specks of dust as the blood from a brāhmaṇa's wound takes up, for so many years, O king, does the offender turn round and round in hell.

sanskrit: bhrūṇahāhavamadhye tu śudhyate śastrapātitaḥ ātmānaṃ juhuyād vahnau samiddhe tena śudhyati
english: The slayer of an embryo is purified by falling beneath weapons in the midst of battle; or he may offer himself up in the kindled fire, and by that he is cleansed.

sanskrit: surāpo vāruṇīm uṣṇāṃ pītvā pāpād vimucyate tayā sa kāye nirdagdhe mṛtyunā pretya śudhyati lokāṃś ca labhate vipro nānyathā labhate hi saḥ
english: The drinker of liquor is freed from his sin by drinking boiling spirituous liquor; his body burned away thereby, he is purified through death in the world beyond, and the brāhmaṇa thus wins the higher worlds, which otherwise he would not win.

sanskrit: gurutalpam adhiṣṭhāya durātmā pāpacetanaḥ sūrmīṃ jvalantīm āśliṣya mṛtyunā sa viśudhyati
english: The evil-souled, wicked-minded man who has defiled his teacher's bed is purified through death by embracing a blazing iron image of a woman.

sanskrit: atha vā śiśnavṛṣaṇāv ādāyāñjalinā svayam nairṛtīṃ diśam āsthāya nipatet sa tv ajihmagaḥ
english: Or else, taking his own organ and testicles in his cupped hands, let him face toward the southwest quarter and fall straight onward, never swerving, until he dies.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇārthe 'pi vā prāṇān saṃtyajet tena śudhyati aśvamedhena vāpīṣṭvā gomedhenāpi vā punaḥ agniṣṭomena vā samyag iha pretya ca pūyate
english: Or he may lay down his life for a brāhmaṇa's sake, and by that he is purified; or by duly performing the Horse Sacrifice, or the Cow Sacrifice, or the Agniṣṭoma, he is cleansed both here and hereafter.

sanskrit: tathaiva dvādaśa samāḥ kapālī brahmahā bhavet brahmacārī cared bhaikṣaṃ svakarmodāharan muniḥ
english: Likewise the slayer of a brāhmaṇa may for twelve years bear a skull, and as a chaste and silent sage go begging his food, proclaiming aloud his own deed.

sanskrit: evaṃ vā tapasā yukto brahmahā savanī bhavet evaṃ vā garbham ajñātā cātreyīṃ yo 'bhigacchati dviguṇā brahmahatyā vai ātreyīvyasane bhavet
english: Thus, joined to austerity, the slayer of a brāhmaṇa may become fit for the sacrifice. And he who, unknowingly, approaches a woman of the line of Atri who is with child incurs twice the guilt of brāhmaṇa-slaying in the ruin of that Ātreyī.

sanskrit: surāpo niyatāhāro brahmacārī kṣamācaraḥ ūrdhvaṃ tribhyo 'tha varṣebhyo yajetāgniṣṭutā param ṛṣabhaikasahasraṃ gā dattvā śubham avāpnuyāt
english: The drinker of liquor, eating sparingly, chaste, and given to forbearance, may after three years sacrifice with the Agniṣṭut as the supreme rite; and by giving a thousand cows together with a bull he attains to blessedness.

sanskrit: vaiśyaṃ hatvā tu varṣe dve ṛṣabhaikaśatāś ca gāḥ śūdraṃ hatvābdam evaikam ṛṣabhaikādaśāś ca gāḥ
english: For slaying a vaiśya, two years of penance and a gift of a hundred cows with a bull; for slaying a śūdra, but a single year, and eleven cows with a bull.

sanskrit: śvabarbarakharān hatvā śaudram eva vrataṃ caret mārjāracāṣamaṇḍūkān kākaṃ bhāsaṃ ca mūṣakam
english: Having killed a dog, a barbarian, or an ass, he should perform the same vow as for a śūdra; and likewise for a cat, a blue jay, a frog, a crow, a vulture, or a mouse.

sanskrit: uktaḥ paśusamo dharmo rājan prāṇinipātanāt prāyaścittāny athānyāni pravakṣyāmy anupūrvaśaḥ
english: Thus has the rule been told, O king, for the killing of creatures, reckoning them as on a level with cattle; now I shall declare the other expiations in their order.

sanskrit: talpe cānyasya caurye ca pṛthak saṃvatsaraṃ caret trīṇi śrotriyabhāryāyāṃ paradāre tu dve smṛte
english: For approaching another's bed and for theft he should perform a year's penance for each; for the wife of a Veda-learned man three years are enjoined, and for another man's wife two.

sanskrit: kāle caturthe bhuñjāno brahmacārī vratī bhavet sthānāsanābhyāṃ viharet trir ahno 'bhyuditād apaḥ evam eva nirācānto yaś cāgnīn apavidhyati
english: Eating only at the fourth mealtime, let him become chaste and bound by his vow, passing his time standing and seated, and bathing thrice a day from sunrise on; so too is it for one who, having failed to rinse his mouth, casts away his sacred fires.

sanskrit: tyajaty akāraṇe yaś ca pitaraṃ mātaraṃ tathā patitaḥ syāt sa kauravya tathā dharmeṣu niścayaḥ
english: And he who, without cause, forsakes his father or his mother becomes a fallen man, O Kaurava; such is the settled rule in matters of law.

sanskrit: grāsācchādanam atyarthaṃ dadyād iti nidarśanam bhāryāyāṃ vyabhicāriṇyāṃ niruddhāyāṃ viśeṣataḥ yat puṃsāṃ paradāreṣu tac caināṃ cārayed vratam
english: The teaching is that to a wife who has gone astray—and especially to one kept in confinement—he should grant ample food and clothing; and the same vow that men perform for going to others' wives, that vow he should cause her to perform.

sanskrit: śreyāṃsaṃ śayane hitvā yā pāpīyāṃsam ṛcchati śvabhis tāṃ khādayed rājā saṃsthāne bahusaṃvṛte
english: The woman who, abandoning a worthier man in her bed, resorts to a baser one—her the king should have devoured by dogs in a public place thronged with people.

sanskrit: pumāṃsaṃ bandhayet prājñaḥ śayane tapta āyase apy ādadhīta dārūṇi tatra dahyeta pāpakṛt
english: The wise king should bind the man upon a bed of heated iron, and should heap on logs beneath, so that the evildoer may be burned away thereon.

sanskrit: eṣa daṇḍo mahārāja strīṇāṃ bhartṛvyatikrame saṃvatsarābhiśastasya duṣṭasya dviguṇo bhavet
english: This, O great king, is the punishment for women who transgress against their husbands; for the wicked man so denounced for a year, it shall be doubled.

sanskrit: dve tasya trīṇi varṣāṇi catvāri sahasevinaḥ kucaraḥ pañca varṣāṇi cared bhaikṣaṃ munivrataḥ
english: Two years for him, three years for one who has consorted thrice, four for him who has long kept such company; and the man of evil ways should beg his food for five years, bound by the vow of a silent sage.

sanskrit: parivittiḥ parivettā yayā ca parividyate pāṇigrāhaś ca dharmeṇa sarve te patitāḥ smṛtāḥ
english: The elder brother passed over in marriage, the younger who marries before him, she through whom he is so passed over, and the priest who joins their hands—all these, by the law, are accounted fallen.

sanskrit: careyuḥ sarva evaite vīrahā yad vrataṃ caret cāndrāyaṇaṃ caren māsaṃ kṛcchraṃ vā pāpaśuddhaye
english: All of these should perform the same vow as the slayer of a hero performs; for a month he should observe the lunar penance, or the kṛcchra, for the cleansing of his sin.

sanskrit: parivettā prayaccheta parivittāya tāṃ snuṣām jyeṣṭhena tv abhyanujñāto yavīyān pratyanantaram enaso mokṣam āpnoti sā ca tau caiva dharmataḥ
english: The younger brother who has married before should give over that bride to the elder who was passed over; but a younger brother who, with the elder's leave, marries next in turn gains release from the sin—both he and she and the elder alike, in accordance with the law.

sanskrit: amānuṣīṣu govarjam anāvṛṣṭir na duṣyati adhiṣṭhātāram attāraṃ paśūnāṃ puruṣaṃ viduḥ
english: As regards beasts other than the human kind—save only the cow—mere defilement entails no sin; for man is known to be the master and consumer of the animals.

sanskrit: paridhāyordhvavālaṃ tu pātram ādāya mṛnmayam caret sapta gṛhān bhaikṣaṃ svakarma parikīrtayan
english: Clad in a skin with the hair turned outward, and bearing a vessel of clay, let him go begging through seven houses, proclaiming aloud his own deed.

sanskrit: tatraiva labdhabhojī syād dvādaśāhāt sa śudhyati caret saṃvatsaraṃ cāpi tad vrataṃ yan nirākṛti
english: Eating only what is gained in that begging, he is purified after twelve days; or he may perform that vow for a full year, which is the rite of one cast out.

sanskrit: bhavet tu mānuṣeṣv evaṃ prāyaścittam anuttamam dānaṃ vādānasakteṣu sarvam eva prakalpayet anāstikeṣu gomātraṃ prāṇam ekaṃ pracakṣate
english: Thus among human cases the highest expiation comes to be; and for those given to liberality he may ordain a gift of any kind whatever; but for unbelievers the loss of even a single cow's life they reckon as enough.

sanskrit: śvavarāhamanuṣyāṇāṃ kukkuṭasya kharasya ca māṃsaṃ mūtrapurīṣaṃ ca prāśya saṃskāram arhati
english: He who has eaten the flesh, the urine, or the dung of a dog, a boar, a man, a cock, or an ass deserves the rite of purification.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇasya surāpasya gandham āghrāya somapaḥ apas tryahaṃ pibed uṣṇās tryaham uṣṇaṃ payaḥ pibet tryaham uṣṇaṃ ghṛtaṃ pītvā vāyubhakṣo bhavet tryaham
english: A soma-drinking brāhmaṇa who has smelled the breath of one who has drunk liquor should drink hot water for three days, hot milk for three days, and hot clarified butter for three days, and then for three days more live upon air alone.

sanskrit: evam etat samuddiṣṭaṃ prāyaścittaṃ sanātanam brāhmaṇasya viśeṣeṇa tattvajñānena jāyate
english: Thus has the eternal rule of expiation been set forth, especially for the brāhmaṇa; yet true purification arises from the knowledge of the truth.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca kathāntaram athāsādya khaḍgayuddhaviśāradaḥ nakulaḥ śaratalpastham idam āha pitāmaham
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, finding a pause in the discourse, Nakula, who was skilled in combat with the sword, spoke thus to the grandsire as he lay upon his bed of arrows.
